steps.question: Given the 12000 x 12 gene-level TPM table (6 psoriasis lesional vs 6 control skin samples, single batch, unpaired), are the samples comparable after log2 transformation — do PCA/hierarchical clustering separate lesional from control, are there outlier samples, and how many genes pass a minimum-expression filter?
acceptance_criteria: log2(TPM+1) matrix produced for all 12 samples with the metadata condition column joined and verified to match sample order
PCA and/or hierarchical clustering plot generated showing lesional vs control separation
A per-gene expression filter (e.g. median log2TPM or proportion of samples with TPM > 1) is applied and reports how many of the 12000 genes are retained
Any outlier sample or batch anomaly is flagged explicitly, not silently dropped

steps.name: limma-trend differential expression, lesional vs control
caveats: TPM-derived DE lacks the count-based mean-variance modeling of DESeq2/edgeR/voom; effect-size (logFC) and significance estimates are more approximate, especially for lowly-expressed genes — state this limitation in the output
n=6 vs 6 is a small, unpaired, single-batch design — no batch correction is applicable, but statistical power is limited and results should not be overclaimed
Do not attempt to reconstruct counts from TPM; do not run DESeq2/edgeR on TPM values as if they were counts
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between psoriasis lesional and control skin samples in the 12000-gene TPM table, using a method valid for expression-only (non-count) input?
acceptance_criteria: log2(TPM+1) matrix (from T1S1, post-filter) modeled with limma: model.matrix on the condition column (lesional vs control), lmFit, then eBayes(trend=TRUE) — NOT voom (voom requires raw counts) and NOT DESeq2/edgeR count-based GLMs
topTable output reports logFC, moderated t, raw P.Value and BH-adjusted adj.P.Val for every retained gene
Full results table (all tested genes, not just significant ones) saved with gene symbols preserved
Report explicitly states this is a limma-trend analysis on TPM-derived log-expression, not a count-based test, and that this is a methodological compromise forced by the missing raw counts
A volcano plot and top-N (e.g. 25-50) gene table highlighting adj.P.Val < 0.05 and |logFC| thresholds are produced

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of the lesional vs control DE gene list
caveats: Gene symbols in the TPM table must be matched exactly (case, aliasing) against GMT gene symbols; unmatched genes should be reported as a count, not silently dropped without note
steps.question: Which WikiPathways and MSigDB Hallmark pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between psoriasis lesional and control skin (from the limma-trend result in T1S2)?
acceptance_criteria: Enrichment run on the significant gene list (e.g. adj.P.Val < 0.05) split by direction (up in lesional, up in control) and/or as a ranked list (by moderated t or logFC) using GSEA-style pre-ranked testing
Uses the WikiPathways human GMT and the MSigDB Hallmark human GMT staged in the environment, matched on HGNC gene symbols consistent with the TPM table's gene-symbol identifiers
Reports enriched pathway name, gene set size, NES/enrichment score, and adjusted P-value for both resources
If either GMT resource is unexpectedly absent at run time, the step reports that gap rather than fabricating pathway results

steps.name: Transcription-factor activity inference from log-TPM expression
caveats: TF activity scores are inferred, not measured directly — they reflect target-gene expression patterns filtered through the regulon, not TF protein activity or phosphorylation state
With n=6 vs 6, per-TF group comparisons have limited power; treat results as hypothesis-generating
steps.question: Which transcription factors show differential inferred activity between psoriasis lesional and control skin samples, based on the log-TPM expression matrix and a curated human TF-target regulon?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the CollecTRI human TF-target regulatory network (source/target/weight) staged in the environment as the prior network
Runs decoupler's univariate linear model (ULM) method on the log2(TPM+1) matrix (from T1S1) per sample to produce a sample x TF activity score matrix
Compares TF activity scores between lesional and control groups (e.g. Wilcoxon or t-test per TF) and reports adjusted P-values
Top differentially active TFs are reported by name with direction of activity change
If the CollecTRI network is unexpectedly absent at run time, the step reports that gap rather than fabricating TF results

plan.title: Psoriasis lesional vs control DE from TPM-only bulk RNA-seq
plan.analytical_narrative: The core delivered only a gene-level TPM table (12000 genes x 12 samples, 6 lesional vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch) with no raw counts and no quantification directories, so count-based tools (DESeq2, edgeR's exact/GLM tests, standard voom which needs a DGEList of counts) cannot be run in their normal form — voom's mean-variance trend is fit against counts, and DESeq2 requires integer counts for its negative-binomial GLM. The standard, literature-grounded way to run differential expression directly on a TPM/expression-only matrix is limma with the 'limma-trend' variant: log2-transform the TPM values (with a small pseudocount), fit a linear model with lmFit, and call eBayes(trend=TRUE) so the empirical Bayes moderation absorbs the mean-variance relationship from the log-expression values themselves rather than from library-size-derived precision weights (Law et al. 2014, Genome Biology, the paper that established the limma/voom precision-weighting framework this trend variant is derived from; documented directly in the Bioconductor GSVA/limma vignettes surfaced in this environment). This avoids the two things TPM-only data cannot support: raw count-based dispersion estimation and voom's count-derived weights. Track 1 does QC/normalization-diagnostics then the limma-trend DE test, track 2 takes the resulting gene list into pathway enrichment (WikiPathways human, MSigDB Hallmark human) grounded in HGNC symbols matching the TPM table's gene-symbol rows, track 3 layers a TF-activity readout (CollecTRI human regulon, decoupler ULM) on the same log-TPM matrix to give a mechanistic, transcription-factor-level view of what is driving the lesional signature, complementing the single-gene DE list. All three tracks operate on the same 12-sample TPM table; no step invents count data or pretends TPM can be converted back to counts.
